title: Windows Let Light Through
objective: Describe how windows let light through and how to protect our eyes.

items.prompt: Maxine looks through four objects toward the sunny yard. Which one lets light through?
items.explanation: Clear glass in a window lets light pass through, so Maxine can see the yard. Metal, wood, and brick block most light.

items.prompt: Milo reads near a bright window. Which action uses light safely?

options.text: Point a flashlight into a friend’s eyes
Look away when the light is too bright
Look directly into a bright bulb

items.explanation: Looking away from glare protects eyes. Staring at the Sun or bright bulbs, or shining a light at eyes, can hurt.

items.prompt: Maxine walks outside on a bright day. Which action protects her eyes?

options.text: Look away from a light that is too bright
Shine a flashlight into a friend’s eyes
Point a lamp at her eyes up close

items.explanation: Looking away from very bright light reduces glare and protects eyes. The other choices direct intense light into eyes.

items.prompt: Sunlight enters a room through a window. Which example shows light behavior?

options.text: A lamp lights a dark room

items.explanation: Clear glass transmits light into the room. Lamps also involve light, while radios and drums make sound.

items.prompt: Maxine sees the garden through a window. Which statement explains what happened?

options.text: A window let light from the garden reach her eyes
A whistle made the glass transparent

items.explanation: Light from the garden passes through clear glass to Maxine’s eyes, allowing her to see. Sound sources do not make glass transparent.
